# ProcessInstance rich audit view, human-task audit model, and autogenerated ids

**Date:** 2026-07-27
**Status:** Design complete — spec + ADR-0144…0149 + plan written and **survived the
rule-#9 adversarial audit** (two Opus auditors; findings adjudicated and folded, see
"Adversarial audit resolutions"). **Ready for implementation** (fresh session).

## Problem

Marshalling a `service.ProcessInstance` today yields a thin projection: the
embedded process **definition template is not included** (only `def_id` /
`def_version` summaries and derived `action_bindings` / `scoped_actions`), the
human-task records carry **no completion or claim audit**, node visits carry no
task linkage or close reason, and the identifiers embedded in the JSON leak the
instance id as a suffix (`<instance_id>-hN`). Consumers embedding the engine
need a **single, self-contained, fully-audited** instance document: the full
definition, who did what and when on every human task, and why each node visit
closed.

This delivery reshapes the marshalled `ProcessInstance` JSON into that document
and adds the supporting engine/persistence data it requires. It is **one
delivery** spanning six ADRs (0144–0149).

## Grounded facts (source-verified 2026-07-27)

- `service.ProcessInstance` is an interface; its JSON is produced by the
  unexported `instanceJSON` / `taskJSON` / `nodeVisitJSON` / `tokenJSON`
  projections in `service/instance.go`. The projection is **write-only** — it is
  never deserialized or persisted, so its shape carries **no stored-data risk**.
- `model.ProcessDefinition` already has a canonical `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON`
  (`definition/model/node_wire.go:148/169`) producing camelCase
  `{id, version, nodes, flows, cancelActions}`. **This same JSON is the persisted
  JSONB** in `wrkflw_definitions.definition`
  (`internal/persistence/store/definitions.go:93/129/165`) — it is the *only*
  (de)serialization vector for definitions.
- Go's `encoding/json` matches keys case-insensitively **only within a single
  token** (`strings.EqualFold`); an inserted underscore is not a fold. Verified:
  stored `"IsDefault"` decodes into `json:"is_default"` as **false** (lost);
  stored `"eligibleRoles"` into `json:"eligible_roles"` as **[]** (lost). ⇒ A
  camelCase→snake_case rename of the persisted definition wire would silently
  corrupt already-stored definitions. **The library is pre-release with no
  deployed data**, so there is nothing to corrupt: we retag the canonical wire to
  snake_case and update all fixtures/golden tests in the same change (no
  migration, no dual-read). This is a deliberate breaking change taken now,
  before release, to keep one consistent format.
- The library follows a discriminator convention: **`kind`** (`NodeWire.Kind`,
  `TriggerWire.Kind`, validate `Kind`, admin DTO `Kind`) and **`state`**
  (lifecycle) — there is **no** `json:"type"` discriminator anywhere. And
  **`outcome`** is the established term for a terminal disposition
  (`TerminationOutcome`, `OutcomeComplete`/`OutcomeAbort`,
  `definition/event/event.go:50`). New names conform to these.
- `humantask.HumanTask` fields: `TaskToken, InstanceID, NodeID, Eligibility,
  Candidates []string, State, ClaimedBy string, CreatedAt, DueAt, Vars`. There is
  **no** completion actor/time/outcome/note, **no** claim timestamp, and candidates
  are **IDs only**. It is persisted both in the instance `snapshot` blob and as
  normalized columns in `wrkflw_human_task` (`humantask_store.go:68`).
- `humantask.ActorResolver.Candidates(ctx, spec, vars)` returns
  **`[]authz.Actor`** (`humantask.go:103`), but the runtime narrows it to
  `Candidates []string` — the rich actors are **discarded** today.
- `authz.Actor` = `{ID string, Roles []string, Attributes map[string]any}`. No
  first-class username/email; those are freeform `Attributes`.
- `engine.NodeVisit` = `{NodeID, TokenID, EnteredAt, LeftAt *time.Time, ActorID
  *string}` (`engine/state.go:134`). `ActorID` is stamped on human completion via
  `setVisitActor` (`step_state.go:150`), matched by `(tokenID, nodeID)`. No task
  linkage, no close reason. Persisted only in the `snapshot` blob (untagged) —
  additive fields are safe.
- Token/task/etc. ids are generated in the **pure engine core** as
  `<InstanceID>-<prefix><seq>`: tokens `-t` (`step_state.go:49/60`), tasks `-h`
  (`:129`), commands `-c` (`:124`), timers `-tm` (`:134`), incidents `-inc`
  (`:141`), scopes `-s` (`state_compensation.go:221`). The format is **generated,
  never parsed** anywhere in prod. The core is deterministic-by-design and
  wall-clock-free, enforced by `engine/purity_test.go` (forbids denied imports +
  `time.Now`-family AST calls).
- Completion API surface (4 layers): `httpcore.CompleteInput{Actor, Output}`
  (`dto.go:44`) → `service.CompleteTaskRequest{TaskToken, Actor, Output}`
  (`request.go:55`) → `TaskService.Complete(ctx, token, actor, output)`
  (`runtime/task/service.go:149`) → `engine.HumanCompleted{TaskToken, Output,
  Actor}` + `NewHumanCompleted(at, token, output, actor)` (`trigger.go:108/133`).
  There is **no** completion type or note anywhere. `handleHumanCompleted`
  already `mergeVars(output)` and has the node definition in scope
  (`step_triggers.go:519/539/544`).
- Claim/reassign already carry the actor and the engine stamps the time
  (`NewHumanClaimed(clk.Now(), …)`), but only `ClaimedBy string` is retained (no
  timestamp, no history). Reassignment overwrites it.
- The transport layer's own `httpcore.NewInstanceView` DTO (`view.go`) has its
  own `def_id`/`def_version` and is **independent** of `instanceJSON`; the
  `service.ProcessInstance` marshalling is consumed by the snapshot endpoint and
  by library consumers embedding the projection.

## Target shape

The canonical target JSON is committed alongside this spec as the reference for
implementation and tests: **`docs/specs/assets/process-instance-sample.json`**
(a running two-stage-approval instance, one human task completed, one claimed and
waiting). All field names below match that file.

### Envelope (`instanceJSON`) — ADR-0144

- **Remove** `action_bindings` (derivable from, or superseded by, the embedded
  definition).
- **Keep** `def_id` and `def_version`, unconditionally. ⚠ *Amended during code
  review (ADR-0144 implementation amendment 1): these were originally slated for
  removal alongside `action_bindings`, but the `definition` embed is `omitempty`,
  so a nil definition left the document with no template identity at all. The
  identity is the stable routing key and comes from the instance state, not from a
  resolved definition.*
- **Add** `definition` — the process definition, marshalled via its **canonical
  (now snake_case) wire** (`ProcessDefinition.MarshalJSON`); the instance view
  embeds it directly (no separate projection). Omitted when the definition is nil.
- The canonical wire gains `scoped_actions` (from `def.ScopedActionNames()`) — a
  new additive field carrying the scoped-action *names* (the catalog itself stays
  unserialized).
- Keep `instance_id`, `status`, `variables`, `tokens`, `history`, `tasks`,
  `started_at`, `ended_at`.

### Definition wire (unified snake_case, JSON + YAML) — ADR-0144

The definition has **one** shape across persisted JSONB, the instance-view embed,
and YAML authoring. `ProcessDefinition.MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON`,
`definitionWire`, `NodeWire`, `TriggerWire`, `flow.SequenceFlow`, the validation
descriptor, and the `nodeYAML`/`definitionYAML`/`sequenceFlowYAML` authoring
structs are all **retagged to snake_case**.

- Object: `{id, version, scoped_actions?, nodes[], flows[], cancel_actions?}`.
- Node: `{id, kind, name?, label?, action?, eligible_roles?, eligible_privileges?,
  outcomes?, expose_outcome?, outcome_variable?, …}` — snake_case, omitempty.
  `kind` VALUE stays lowerCamelCase (`startEvent`) — an enum value, not a key.
  `label` is the explicit label only (Name fallback resolved in-memory, ADR-0139).
- Flow: `{id, source, target, condition?, is_default?}` — snake_case; `condition`
  and `is_default` omitted when empty (`flow.SequenceFlow` gains json tags).
- **Breaking, taken now (pre-release):** all wire/YAML fixtures and golden
  round-trip tests are updated to snake_case in the same change; there is no
  deployed data and therefore no migration. A golden decode test pins the new
  snake_case shape.

### Tokens (`tokenJSON`) — shape unchanged, state names renamed — ADR-0145

`{id, node_id, state, scope_id?, payload?, entered_at, retry_attempts?}`. Tokens
are the live execution frontier (see "why tokens" below); no cancelled state
exists by design (cancelled tokens are consumed/removed, not tombstoned).

**Token-state rename (Go constants + wire values).** For clarity and consistency
(and because `TokenWaitingCommand` over-narrows — a parked token awaits a command,
signal, *or* message):

| Go constant | was → now | wire value was → now |
|---|---|---|
| `TokenActive` | (unchanged) | `active` (unchanged) |
| `TokenWaitingCommand` → `TokenWaiting` | renamed | `waitingCommand` → `waiting` |
| `TokenAtJoin` → `TokenJoining` | renamed | `atJoin` → `joining` |
| `TokenIncident` | (unchanged) | `incident` (unchanged) |

The wire strings are produced solely by `tokenStateString` (`service/instance.go`);
the constant rename is mechanical across the engine core (~28 files). Breaking,
taken pre-release.

### History (`nodeVisitJSON`) — ADR-0145

- `{node_id, token_id, entered_at, left_at?, task_id?, close_kind?}`.
- **Remove** `actor_id` (resolve the actor from the linked task instead).
- **Add** `task_id` — present on **userTask** visits (open or closed), linking
  the visit to its `tasks` entry. Backed by a new `NodeVisit.TaskToken` field set
  when the task is minted.
- **Add** `close_kind` — the reason the visit closed; **omitted for normal
  `completed` closes**, emitted only for abnormal closes. Value set:
  `instance_cancelled`, `boundary_interrupted`, `terminated`, `compensated`,
  `reversed`, `errored`. Backed by a new `NodeVisit` close-reason field stamped at
  each `consumeToken`/terminal site.

### Tasks (`taskJSON`) — ADR-0147

- `{task_id, node_id, state, candidates[], claim?, created_at, due_at?, completion?}`.
- **Rename** `task_token` → `task_id` (JSON key only; the engine "task token"
  concept is unchanged).
- **Remove** `claimed_by`; **add** `claim?` — a single `{actor, timestamp}` object
  (omitted while Unclaimed). One claimant at a time; no history (matches engine).
- `candidates[]` — array of **actor** objects (not id strings).
- **Add** `completion?` — `{actor, timestamp, outcome?, note?}` (omitted until
  Completed). `outcome` is the chosen completion outcome; `note` is the actor note.

### Actor object (passthrough) — ADR-0147

Everywhere an actor appears (`candidates[]`, `claim.actor`, `completion.actor`):
```
{ "id": "...", "roles": [...], "attributes": { ... } }
```
Faithful passthrough of `authz.Actor` — lossless, convention-free, maximally
flexible for consumers. `username`/`email` appear under `attributes` only if the
consumer's `ActorResolver` populated them; the engine does not guarantee them.

## Design decisions

### 1. Unify the definition on one snake_case canonical wire — ADR-0144

Because the library is **pre-release with no deployed data**, the original reason
for a view-only projection (avoiding silent corruption of stored camelCase
definitions) no longer applies. We instead retag the **canonical** definition wire
to snake_case so persisted JSONB, the instance-view embed, and YAML authoring all
share **one** shape — no projection, no duplicated field mapping to keep in sync.
`ProcessDefinition.MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON`, `definitionWire`, `NodeWire`,
`TriggerWire`, `flow.SequenceFlow` (gains json tags), the validation descriptor,
and the YAML authoring structs are retagged together; all fixtures and golden
round-trip tests are updated in the same change. The instance view then embeds the
definition via its canonical `MarshalJSON`.

### 2. `outcomes` declaration + fail-closed validation — ADR-0146

- User tasks gain an optional `outcomes []string` declaring the accepted
  completion outcomes. Additive field in the (now snake_case) `NodeWire` as
  `outcomes`, round-tripped through `nodeYAML` and validation. Empty = no
  constraint (a bare completion with no `outcome` is allowed).
- The chosen `outcome` is validated **in `handleHumanCompleted`** (engine, fail-
  closed) against the node's `outcomes`, with a new sentinel `ErrInvalidOutcome`
  beside the existing `ErrManualTaskPayload`. No completion path (including durable
  replay) can bypass it. When `outcomes` is empty, any/no `outcome` is accepted.

### 3. Completion API refactor (`outcome` + `note`) — ADR-0146

Thread two new fields through all four layers via an engine-side value object:
```go
// engine
type Completion struct { Outcome string; Note string; Output map[string]any }
func NewHumanCompleted(at time.Time, taskToken string, c Completion, actor authz.Actor) HumanCompleted
```
- `HumanCompleted` gains `Outcome`, `Note` (in addition to `Output`, `Actor`).
- `TaskService.Complete(ctx, token, actor, c Completion)`.
- `service.CompleteTaskRequest` gains `Outcome`, `Note`.
- `httpcore.CompleteInput` gains `outcome`, `note` JSON fields.
- Durable trigger envelope (`trigger_codec.go`) gains **additive omitempty**
  fields ⇒ backward-safe for already-persisted commands/timers.
- Claim and reassign APIs are **unchanged** (actor already flows; timestamp
  engine-stamped) — only state recording changes.

### 4. Outcome → variable exposure (hybrid opt-in) — ADR-0146

`completion.outcome` is **always** recorded as audit. Variable exposure is an
orthogonal opt-in on the user-task node, resolved with explicit-name precedence:
```
if node.OutcomeVariable != "":  vars[node.OutcomeVariable] = outcome   // explicit name wins
else if node.ExposeOutcome:      vars[node.ID + "_outcome"] = outcome   // convention
else:                            (audit-only)
```
Applied **after** the `Output` merge in `handleHumanCompleted`. The exposed value
is the **outcome string** (`"approve"`); gateway conditions compare strings
(`manager_review_outcome == "approve"`). Two new optional user-task fields:
`ExposeOutcome bool` (wire `expose_outcome`) and `OutcomeVariable string` (wire
`outcome_variable`).

### 5. Human-task audit model + persistence — ADR-0147 / ADR-0148

- `humantask.HumanTask`: `Candidates []string` → `Candidates []authz.Actor`
  (stop discarding resolver output); `ClaimedBy string` → `Claim *Claim` where
  `Claim = {Actor authz.Actor; At time.Time}` (nullable); add completion audit
  `Completion *Completion` where `Completion = {Actor authz.Actor; At time.Time;
  Outcome, Note string}`.
- The engine records: the resolved actors on task creation
  (`userTaskStrategy.enter`), the claim `{actor, at}` on `HumanClaimed`, and the
  completion `{actor, at, outcome, note}` on `HumanCompleted`.
- **Persistence (ADR-0148):** the `snapshot` blob change is additive/free. The
  normalized `wrkflw_human_task` store gains new columns so admin task queries see
  the audit: `candidates` (rich JSON, replacing the id-only column), `claim`
  (JSON, nullable), `completion` (JSON, nullable) — one migration across
  Postgres/MySQL/SQLite. Exact column strategy (widen existing
  `candidates`/`claimed_by` vs add JSON columns) decided in ADR-0148; the store
  read/write (`Upsert`, `scanTask`, column list `:68`) updated accordingly. A
  round-trip test pins the new column shape (pre-release ⇒ no old-row migration).

### 6. Autogenerated ids via injected port — ADR-0149

- Add an **`IDGen` seam** to `StepOptions` (`func() (string, error)`, or a small
  interface). The pure core **calls** it during stepping — no `xid`/wall-clock
  import in the core ⇒ `engine/purity_test.go` still passes (the generator lives
  in the runtime/service layer).
- **Default = deterministic counter** (`<instance>-<prefix><seq>`). When `IDGen`
  is nil, behaviour is byte-identical to today ⇒ engine-core tests and replay stay
  deterministic.
- The **service/runtime construction wires `idgen.XID()`** as the default `IDGen`,
  so real product instances get opaque autogenerated ids (the requested behavior)
  while the core keeps its invariants.
- Applies to all seven generation sites (tokens, tasks, commands, timers,
  incidents, scopes). ~18 runtime/service test files that assert the `-tN`/`-hN`
  format at the full-stack level are updated; pure-engine tests using the default
  counter are unaffected. Id format is never parsed, so no structural dependency
  breaks.

## Why `tokens` exists (design note captured for the audit)

Tokens are the engine's **live execution frontier** — the set of active loci of
control ("program counters"). All four `TokenState` values are live (`active`,
`waiting`, `joining`, `incident`). A consumed/cancelled/terminated token is
**removed** from the set (`consumeToken`, `step_state.go:191`), not marked — hence
no `cancelled` state. Cancellation is recorded at three other levels: instance
`status`, task `state` (`cancelled`), and the visit's `left_at` + new `close_kind`.
This is why the completion/claim audit lives on `tasks`/`history`, never on
`tokens`.

## ADR breakdown (one delivery)

| ADR | Scope |
|---|---|
| 0144 | Unify definition on one snake_case canonical wire (JSONB + view embed + YAML); envelope changes (drop `action_bindings`, keep `def_id`/`def_version`, embed `definition`); `scoped_actions` in wire; `task_id` rename |
| 0145 | `NodeVisit` enrichment — `task_id` link + `close_kind` at every terminal/consume site; remove history `actor_id`; token-state rename (`TokenWaiting`/`TokenJoining` + wire `waiting`/`joining`) |
| 0146 | `UserTask.outcomes` + fail-closed validation; completion API refactor (`outcome`/`note`); hybrid outcome-exposure opt-in |
| 0147 | HumanTask audit model — `Claim`, rich `Candidates []authz.Actor`, `Completion`; passthrough actor shape |
| 0148 | Persistence — new `wrkflw_human_task` columns + migration (Postgres/MySQL/SQLite); golden-fixture guard |
| 0149 | Engine id-generation — injected `IDGen` port; deterministic counter default; `xid` wired at the product boundary |

## Verification checklist

- [ ] `service.ProcessInstance` marshals to the target shape; nil-definition omits
      `definition`; `scoped_actions` appears inside `definition`.
- [ ] Definition wire is snake_case across JSONB storage, the view embed, and YAML;
      `flows` use `id/source/target` with `condition`/`is_default` omitted when
      empty; a golden round-trip test pins the snake_case shape and all wire/YAML
      fixtures are updated.
- [ ] `outcomes` round-trips through `NodeWire` (snake_case) + YAML + validation; a
      completion `outcome` outside the set is rejected with `ErrInvalidOutcome`;
      empty `outcomes` accepts any/no `outcome`.
- [ ] Completion `outcome`/`note` flow transport→service→runtime→engine and land in
      `completion`; durable trigger envelope round-trips the new fields.
- [ ] Outcome exposure: `outcome_variable` wins; else `expose_outcome` uses
      `<node_id>_outcome`; else no variable; applied after `Output`; audit always
      recorded.
- [ ] History userTask visits carry `task_id`; `close_kind` emitted only for
      abnormal closes with the correct value per terminal path; `actor_id` gone.
- [ ] `tasks` carry rich `candidates`, singular `claim{actor,timestamp}`, and
      `completion{actor,timestamp,outcome,note}`; actor is passthrough
      `{id,roles,attributes}`.
- [ ] New `wrkflw_human_task` columns persist and read back the audit across
      Postgres/MySQL/SQLite (testcontainers); a golden old-row test passes.
- [ ] Token states rename cleanly: `TokenWaiting`/`TokenJoining` across the engine
      core; `tokenStateString` emits `waiting`/`joining`; `active`/`incident`
      unchanged; all references and tests updated.
- [ ] `IDGen` port: nil default is byte-identical to today (core tests green,
      purity test green); service/runtime default emits `xid` ids; all seven id
      sites covered.
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` green; per-touched-package coverage ≥ 85% with hot
      paths (completion handler, id generation, projection marshalling,
      persistence round-trip) covered first; `golangci-lint` clean.

## Adversarial audit resolutions (2026-07-27, rule #9 — two Opus auditors)

> **⚠ SUPERSEDED IN PART (2026-07-27, session 3):** resolution **B1** below is
> **retired** — see ADR-0147 "Implementation amendments" #1. Candidates are
> resolved **before** the parking commit; they are *not* written into `st.Tasks`
> from the post-commit `perform`, which cannot persist them. Read that amendment
> before acting on B1.

All accepted unless marked. These are **binding on implementation**; the plan
phases are amended to match.

**Blockers**

- **B1 — Rich `candidates` never reach the rendered view (recording site wrong).**
  Verified: `userTaskStrategy.enter` (`engine/step_nodes.go:607`) is pure and sets
  **no** candidates; the runtime resolves `[]authz.Actor` in
  `runtime/processdriver_action.go:257` and writes them **only** to
  `driver.tasks.Upsert` (line 290) — **never back into `st.Tasks`** (line 286 only
  *reads* `TaskByToken` for NodeID/CreatedAt). The instance view marshals
  `st.Tasks`, so candidates would render empty. **Fix:** the runtime's `AwaitHuman`
  path must write the resolved rich `[]authz.Actor` **back into `st.Tasks[i]`** (the
  persisted snapshot), not only the task store. Correct ADR-0147's recording-site
  attribution from `userTaskStrategy.enter` to `runtime/processdriver_action.go`.
- **B2 — Sample vs ADR-0149 id contradiction.** The sample previously showed
  counter-format `-t1`/`-h1` ids while ADR-0149 wires `xid` to all id sites.
  **Resolved:** the user requires all ids autogenerated (not instance-suffixed), so
  ADR-0149 stands; the **sample is regenerated with opaque xid-shaped token/task
  ids**, and Plan 8.4's whole-document test **injects a deterministic `IDGen`** (so
  the oracle is stable) while product uses `xid`. State this in Plan 8.4.

**Majors**

- **M-clone — deep-copy the audit state.** Two clone sites copy `Candidates` as
  `[]string` and will share nested maps/pointees after the type change:
  `engine/step_state.go:304` `cloneState` (Step-purity guard) and
  `persistence/caching_task_store.go:126` `cloneTask`. Both must deep-copy each
  actor's `Roles`/`Attributes` and the `*Claim`/`*Completion` pointees. Hot path —
  cover first.
- **M-readers — two packages missing from the blast radius.** `persistence`
  (`caching_task_store.go`) and `runtime/view` (`instance_actionable.go:33,87` —
  `ActionableTask{Candidates []string, ClaimedBy}`) both compile-break on the
  `HumanTask` type change and are in no phase. Add both. **Decision:** migrate
  `runtime/view.ActionableTask` to the consistent shape (`task_id`, rich
  `candidates`, `claim`) so the library does not ship two divergent task JSON
  shapes.
- **M-retag — retag set incomplete.** Nested wire structs with **no** json tags are
  left PascalCase and reinstate the mixed-casing wart: `model.RetryPolicy`
  (`definition/model/retry.go`) and `schedule.ClockTime`
  (`definition/schedule/trigger.go:26`, on `TriggerWire.AtTimes`). Add both (and
  audit for any other nested untagged wire struct) to the Phase-1 retag.
- **M-fixtures — `definition/kinds` golden breaks, unlisted.**
  `definition/kinds/kinds_test.go` `TestGoldenRoundTrip` reads
  `definition/testdata/golden_definition.json` (camelCase + PascalCase flows) and
  asserts byte-identical. Add that file + the `definition/kinds` package to Phase 1.
- **M-processtest — token rename touches `processtest/`.** `TokenWaitingCommand` is
  referenced in `processtest/harness.go` and `processtest/park.go`. Add
  `processtest` to Phase 2's packages and verify command. (Union of files touched by
  the two constants is **29**, not "engine core only".)
- **M-close_kind — enumerate per call site; stamp at the site, not in
  `consumeToken`.** `consumeToken`/`closeVisit` fire on many **normal** paths
  (gateways, joins, subprocess entry) — those must leave `close_kind` **unset**.
  Stamp only at the named terminal sites. Add **`deadline_expired`** to the value
  set (human-task deadline-breach reroute). Classify: error caught by a boundary →
  `boundary_interrupted`; uncaught error end → `errored`; terminate end →
  `terminated`; non-interrupting boundary does **not** close the host visit (no
  stamp). Enumerate the mapping per site in Plan 3.2.
- **M-idgen-layer — no core→runtime inversion.** Define the `IDGen` seam **locally
  in `engine`** (`type IDGen func() (string, error)` or a one-method interface);
  `runtime` adapts `idgen.Generator` to it. Do **not** alias `runtime/idgen` in the
  engine (it compiles and passes `purity_test.go` but violates the layering). Add
  `/runtime/` to `deniedEngineImports` to enforce it.
- **M-manual — manual wait-mode task must fail-closed on outcome/note.** The guard
  at `engine/step_triggers.go:539` checks only `len(Output) > 0`; extend it to also
  reject a non-empty `outcome`/`note` **before** the outcome-set validation (else a
  manual task with no `outcomes` silently accepts them).

**Minors (accepted)**

- `scoped_actions` is **derived / marshal-only** (dropped on unmarshal); the golden
  test must be **marshal-side only** (build in Go → marshal → compare), never
  `JSON→struct→JSON` equality. Documented in ADR-0144.
- **7 id-generation sites / 6 id kinds** (tokens minted at `step_state.go:49` **and**
  `:60`). Reconcile the "six/seven" wording everywhere.
- **Observability:** add a counter for `ErrInvalidOutcome` rejections, a
  `close_kind`-labelled abnormal-termination metric, and `slog`/trace on `IDGen`
  errors (CLAUDE.md observability requirement).
- Snapshot write-amplification from rich candidates in `st.Tasks` is an accepted,
  documented trade-off (the view needs them in the snapshot — see B1).
- Corrected line refs: `ActorResolver.Candidates` `humantask.go:103`;
  `TaskService.Complete` `runtime/task/service.go:149`. `NewHumanCompleted` callers:
  **~24 test + 2 prod** (incl. `internal/persistence/store/trigger_codec.go:142`).
  ADR-0144's "instance_test.go does not assert the removed keys" is **wrong** — it
  asserts `action_bindings` absent (`:51`); that assertion is updated.
- "Id format never parsed" is qualified: the `evtgw:` **await-command** prefix is
  prefix-matched (`step_cancel.go:28`) but is orthogonal to id generation.

## Non-goals

- No dual-format or back-compat for definitions — the snake_case wire is a clean
  pre-release break; fixtures are rewritten, no migration/dual-read is provided.
- No claim/reassignment **history** (single current claim only).
- No engine-guaranteed actor profile fields — `username`/`email` are consumer-
  supplied `Attributes` surfaced verbatim.
- No BPMN2 XML; no new transport endpoints (existing complete/claim endpoints gain
  fields only).
